correctness.rationale: The necessary-and-sufficient systematic parity-subset characterization follows by forcing one singleton recovery and writing unique systematic companions. The verifier enumerates all 65536 parity matrices and independently tests all three disjoint physical-column recovery sets with full subset sums; results agree exactly. Each of the 7800 solutions passes all twenty independent three-batch recovery tests. Exhaustive orbit canonicalization under the declared group yields 26 classes and is independently cross-checked by Burnside sum 14976. Rank and Lemma 7 incidence counts and the complete 26-row representative table are recreated from the same finite universe. Separate exhaustion excludes r<=3 parity columns.

originality.rationale: Existing sources determine optimal length and exhibit optimal systematic 3-PIR/3-batch constructions. The new, narrower claim classifies all physically labeled systematic [I4|P] optimal presentations (7800), their 26 exact S4xS4 equivalence classes, the universal 3-batch property across the equality layer, and the quantitative failure of the 2015 sufficient incidence condition for 7344 instances. Direct full-text comparison with the canonical sources did not find or imply these equality counts.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial four-message, three-server systematic PIR equality layer is a natural optimal-size classification, not an ad hoc code slice. It reveals that every optimal systematic three-PIR presentation is also three-batch, an all-extremizers assertion stronger than known existence theorems, and measures precisely the weakness of a classical sufficient combinatorial-design test (only 456/7800 optima). The 26 orbits and explicit reproducible representatives provide a canonical basis for small PIR/batch code classification and construction analysis.
